title: Redevelopment Results
description:
Six months since you decided to invest in the redevelopment zone.
Today a text came in about a general assembly meeting.
A briefing on the project's current status, apparently.

choices.text: Attend the assembly
choices.result_text:
The room was full of unit holders.
The key point: the project timeline was being extended by two more years.
Real estate wasn't numbers — it was time.
For now, there was nothing to do but wait.

choices.text: Skip it. Just wait for the outcome.
choices.result_text:
You didn't go.
The timeline extension came later by text.
If you invest, you show up.
Ownership shows up at the assembly too.

title: The Quant Was Right
description:
That day you decided to strip out emotion and run on math alone.
A year has passed.
You tallied up the returns.
Slightly above market average.

choices.text: Refine this approach further
choices.result_text:
You added two more variables.
The backtest improved a bit.
Cutting emotion doesn't guarantee profit.
But it does cut mistakes — that was right.

choices.text: It worked — scale up the bet
choices.result_text:
You scaled up.
The market wobbled next quarter.
Even when the math is right — sizing up lets psychology back in.
Quant can lose big too.

title: The Value of Paid Information
description:
Three months since you subscribed to the stock tip sheet.
30,000 won a month.
You followed the picks for three months.
Time to add up the results.

choices.text: Cancel the subscription
choices.result_text:
Three months: 2 wins, 3 losses.
Including the subscription fee — it was negative.
People who sell information make money from subscriptions, not the picks.
Now you knew the difference.

choices.text: Watch a bit longer
choices.result_text:
Watched one more month.
Similar results.
It wasn't that there are no good tip sheets — the approach of following picks blindly was the problem.

title: The End of a Winning Day
description:
That day at the track when you won but didn't stop.
You ended up giving back the whole day's profit before you left.
On the subway home you replayed it.

choices.text: Make "stop when you're up" a rule
choices.result_text:
You wrote it down.
'Walk out when you're winning.'
Giving back profits after a win — that's the most common pattern in gambling.
No rule means emotions decide.

choices.text: Just an unlucky day
choices.result_text:
You called it an unlucky day.
But the same pattern repeated.
Call a pattern luck — and it never changes.

title: The Day of the First Bet
description:
Three months since the day you placed your first bet at the track.
That feeling you had then — it still comes back.
Not sure if it's a good memory or a bad one.

choices.text: Analyze what that feeling actually was
choices.result_text:
Excitement. A sense of control. And an illusion.
Those three mixed together — that was gambling's pull.
Once you name it, the pull eases a little.
Just a little.

choices.text: It was just fun
choices.result_text:
It was fun.
Fun isn't inherently bad.
But where that fun leads — that's something you had to know yourself.

title: Six Months at the Startup
description:
Six months since you joined the startup.
Today the founder asked:
"How is it? Glad you came?"

choices.text: Be honest. "Hard — but I'm learning."
choices.result_text:
The founder smiled. 'Everyone says that at six months.'
Strangely reassuring.
If six months is the hardest part — it also meant you should keep going.

choices.text: Just say "It's good."
choices.result_text:
The founder said '...Really?'
'Sort of,' you said.
It had been a place where you could have been honest.

title: Negotiation Result
description:
Two months since you brought up the salary negotiation first.
No conclusion at the time.
Today HR sent the final answer.

choices.text: It went up — small but it means something
choices.result_text:
200,000 won/month increase.
A number that wouldn't have existed if you hadn't asked.
No one raises it without you speaking up.
That wasn't negotiation — that was just how employment works.

choices.text: No — but asking was right
choices.result_text:
'Not possible this time' was the answer.
No raise — but after raising it once, the next conversation shifted.
Without speaking up, there wouldn't have been a chance either.

title: Was Leaving Right?
description:
Three months since you left thinking something better was out there.
Still haven't landed a new position.
Today your old colleague reached out.
"Hey — the team lead changed. The whole vibe is different now."

choices.text: "Is it? I kind of regret leaving."
choices.result_text:
You felt the pang.
But there was no way to know the team lead would change back then.
Regretting a decision made without information, once the information arrives — that's not fair to yourself.

choices.text: "The team lead wasn't the only reason I left."
choices.result_text:
'It wasn't just the team lead,' you said.
Your colleague said '...Fair enough.'
Even if conditions change — the reasons you left remain.

title: The Flea Market Connection
description:
Half a year since you chatted with the person at the next stall at the flea market.
You exchanged numbers — but the contact has just been sitting in your phone.
Today their name crossed your mind.

choices.text: Reach out. "How have you been?"
choices.result_text:
They were glad to hear from you.
You had a short call.
A small message kept a small connection alive.
Relationships stay with the people who tend them.

choices.text: Leave it. Everyone's busy living.
choices.result_text:
You left it.
The number stayed unsaved.
It became a contact that might get a call someday — or might not.

title: What the Driver Said
description:
The late-night taxi driver and what he said.
"When I was young, I thought I'd make it to Gangnam too."
Facing a tough decision today — those words surfaced again.

choices.text: Use it as a compass for this decision
choices.result_text:
You decided not to give up.
You didn't want to be in a cab someday saying the same thing.
That remark had become a compass.

choices.text: He and I are different.
choices.result_text:
Different.
Different situation, different era.
But the ending of giving up — looked the same either way.

title: Three Months After Treatment
description:
Three months since you went to the doctor when your body wasn't right.
You kept up with the medication.
Today you went in for the follow-up.

choices.text: Improved — keep managing it
choices.result_text:
The doctor said 'Much better.'
Keeping it up was right.
Your body stays with the people who look after it.

choices.text: Not quite there — more care needed
choices.result_text:
A bit more was needed, apparently.
You decided to keep going.
Your body has to hold up for everything else to happen.

title: That Floor Plan and Now
description:
A year since you went to the Gangnam apartment open house.
The unit you saw then. The asking price you heard.
Today you looked up the actual transaction price for that complex.

choices.text: Calculate how much the gap has closed
choices.result_text:
The asking price went up. Your assets went up.
Whether the gap closed or widened — it cut both ways.
But a year ago you couldn't even run the calculation.
Being able to calculate — meant getting closer.

choices.text: Still too far. Just close it.
choices.result_text:
You closed it.
Still far.
But a year ago you were thinking the same thing.
A year passed anyway.

title: What Became of That Neighbor
description:
The neighbor at the gosiwon who motivated you.
Half a year later, their room is empty.
You heard from the ajumma in the shared kitchen:
"That person moved out. Got a new place."

choices.text: Think about the day you'll leave this room too
choices.result_text:
You passed the room.
It was empty.
Gosiwon is a place you pass through.
They passed through first — and you'd pass through too.

choices.text: Wish I'd had their number
choices.result_text:
No number.
Not even a name.
That's what gosiwon was.
But the fact that they'd been a source of drive — that stayed.

title: The Late Return
description:
A month since you finally returned the envelope, late as it was.
Today a short text from them:
'Thank you. I think I'll remember this for a long time.'

choices.text: Reply: "I'm sorry it was so late."
choices.result_text:
'I'm sorry it took so long.'
They replied 'No — you returned it.'
Late and not at all — are different things.

choices.text: Just send an emoji
choices.result_text:
You sent an emoji.
They sent one back.
No words needed — some things were understood between you.

title: That Envelope
description:
Four months since you kept the envelope.
Today you spotted a similar-looking one on the street.
Just a passing envelope — but the memory surfaced.

choices.text: It's not too late. Return it.
choices.result_text:
You tracked down their contact and sent it.
'About that envelope. Late, but here it is.'
They went quiet a moment, then: '...Thank you.'
Late was still the right call.

choices.text: Too late now. Live with it.
choices.result_text:
You called it too late.
But the moment you think it's too late — is actually the earliest moment.
This would keep nagging.

title: After the Lucky Call
description:
A call came at exactly the right moment.
Thanks to it, an opportunity opened up.
Today you met that person for the second time.

choices.text: Build on this connection
choices.result_text:
The second meeting promised a third.
Luck opened the first door.
After that, skill and attitude opened the rest.
That order was right.

choices.text: Use this opportunity and leave it there
choices.result_text:
You used the opportunity and didn't extend it further.
Connections can also be closed by choice.
That wasn't wrong.
